sections.what: Crisis Intervention of Houston provides free, anonymous crisis counseling through telephone and teen text services. Trained volunteers listen, help callers stabilize emotionally and connect them with other support. Its programs also include suicide-bereavement groups, education and community crisis response.
sections.monitoring: Latest read FY2024 original repeats 35,812 calls, texts and chats explicitly for FY2022–2023; Part III repeats 33,521 for FY2021–2022. These are historical contact volumes, not current unique adult households or additional safety outcomes. Current cumulative claims are not annualized. Request distinct adult callers, repeat contact, referral completion, alternative 988 uptake, distress follow-up, privacy/escalation harms and volunteer hours.
sections.qualitative: Original returns distinguish dated contacts from current annual accounting costs. Direct conversation and referral provide a concrete short-term distress mechanism. Current local services offer another route to support alongside national and community alternatives. Contacts are not unique callers, completed treatment or measured deaths prevented. 988 and other services may substitute for much of the modeled annual response. Unrecognized volunteer and partner opportunity costs could materially change the low accounting-cost reference. Original Form 990 verifies EIN 74-2076682. Current recipient-owned Get Involved page contains a PayPal donation form, not a verified checkout transaction or payee restriction. Historical filing/reinstatement questions require donor due diligence, not an assumption that current operations are zero.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $15.38 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 0.106330 clinical QALYs and 0.012011 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.006503 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $181,993. Historical 35,812 contacts are a reference transferred to latest annual cost. Judged .2 distinct adult-household mapping times .15 additional annual response beyond 988, other hotlines and community support yields 1,074.36 exposed household proxies. Clinical .3 short-term meaningful distress improvement times .02 utility for .02 finite year is a weak hypothesis, not a fixed-call suicide-save claim. Full one-off .00001 clinical harm per exposure allows inappropriate escalation or privacy effects. Independent .05 resource success receives $100 net avoided work disruption or usable referral-linked resources after tax, benefit and other-provider offsets; positive overlap .5 then full $2 call/time/process burden gives $48 net, while others lose $2. No survivor earnings or free-service retail price is counted. Union 1074.3600000000001 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 322.30800000000005; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $20,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Trained volunteer time is not fully in recognized tax expense. A $500,000 economic-cost hypothesis and separate external-provider burden stress show that apparent accounting cheapness is not complete social cost. Recipient expense and external unpaid opportunity costs are not the same cost twice. Payer/displaced-beneficiary incidence remains unknown; a referral does not automatically create net social resources. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: FY2024 original recognized tax expense $181,993; FY2023 $181,602; FY2022 $226,567, all twelve-month June fiscal years. No populated event, rental or inventory expense addback recovered. Schedule D requests returned HTTP 404 rather than evidence of zero donated services. Unrecognized volunteers and partner care remain unknown. Historical FY2022–2023 contacts paired with FY2024 cost are an explicit mismatch. Whole-recipient cost versus this narrow hotline hypothesis is not a complete portfolio EV or verified marginal offer.

model.costScope: Whole recognized annual tax recipient expense versus narrow historical hotline channel; unpaid/partner resources unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Local Houston reference with .9 judged MSA share; callers and teens not verified local adult households
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, other hotlines, 911 when appropriate, community mental health and family support retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional short-term stabilization and useful support linkage; contacts not deaths prevented
